task: Make fake_claims() ignore a trailing parenthetical annotation on a claim, so annotated claims with a matching Bash call are receipted, while claims whose command words never appear stay flagged.

global.constraints: Literal request only: change autopilot/receipts.py only. Do not edit tests/test_receipts.py or tests/test_receipts_annotation.py. Use only the standard library. The full suite must still pass with python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

items.goal: In autopilot/receipts.py, strip a trailing parenthetical note (e.g. ' (denied, not executed)') from a claim before matching in fake_claims(), so the claim is receipted when the command words appear in a Bash tool_use. Still flag a claim whose command words never appear. Reported claim strings for flagged fakes keep their original text.

target.value: 0 failures in the new annotation tests (3 tests) and the existing test_receipts.py tests (3 tests)
target.state: proven (new test fails today with 1 failure; existing receipts tests pass today)

items.interfaces: fake_claims(claims: list[str], cmds: list[str]) -> list[str] signature unchanged; matches() and tokens() behavior unchanged for non-annotated input.
items.notes: Only a trailing '(...)' group at the end of the claim is stripped; parentheses elsewhere in the claim are left alone. The judge runs only the two receipts test files because the full suite takes about 38s; the full suite (python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .) should still pass after the change.

judge.cmd: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -p 'test_receipts_annotation.py' && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -p 'test_receipts.py'

next_rung: Normalize other self-report annotations (trailing '# comment', '-> exit 0', or '[...]' notes) and extract this claim cleaning into a shared helper used by both fake_claims and any other consumer of commands_run.
